mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S 350 or S 450 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M276 engine for the S 350 costs £3,200-£4,500 supply-only; a rebuilt M256 engine for the S 450 costs £4,200-£5,400 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity - both engines require specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes S 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start lasting a few seconds is the classic warning sign on the M276 V6 engine. The hydraulic secondary chain tensioners can lose oil pressure, allowing chain slack.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S 450 engine (M256) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M256 inline-six is a modern, sophisticated engine, but it has known wiring harness degradation issues and 48V system vulnerabilities. With these addressed, the engine is proving durable.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S 350 and S 450 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M276 V6 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. The M256 is too new for definitive long-term data, but with proactive maintenance, 100,000+ miles is achievable.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S 350 or S 450 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S-Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt M276 costs £3,200-£4,500 - far less than replacing an £8,000-£18,000 vehicle. The S 450's higher value (£35,000-£60,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S 350 or S 450 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M276 V6 requires approximately 7.5 litres; the M256 inline-six requires approximately 8.0 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 350/450 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S 350 debuted with the W221 generation in 2011 as a mid-cycle upgrade, powered by the M276 3.5-litre V6 petrol producing 306hp - a significant leap over the previous M272 unit. This naturally aspirated V6 featured BlueDIRECT direct injection and MSI multi-spark ignition for improved efficiency and power. In 2020, the W223 S 450 introduced the M256 3.0-litre inline-six with 48V EQ Boost mild-hybrid technology, delivering 367hp and representing a major shift toward electrified flagship mobility.

milestones.description: M276.950, 3.5L naturally aspirated V6, 306hp @ 6,500rpm (S 350, W221 facelift)
2017 - M276.952, 3.0L twin-turbo V6, S 450 (W222, certain markets)
M256.930, 3.0L turbocharged inline-six with 48V EQ Boost, 367hp (S 450, W223)

items.title: 3.5L Naturally Aspirated V6 (2011-2013)
items.commonFailure: Timing chain tensioner wear causing cold-start rattle - the M276 V6 has hydraulic secondary chain tensioners that can leak oil pressure, causing a metallic rattle on startup. M276 engines with engine numbers below a certain threshold may require updated tensioners and check valves per Mercedes TSB LI05.10-P-056435. Oil cooler seal degradation and coolant leaks from hoses are also common.

items.title: 3.0L Turbocharged Inline-Six with 48V EQ Boost (2020-present)
items.commonFailure: Ignition coil wiring harness degradation and 48V system issues - the M256's ignition coil wiring harness sits close to the turbocharger, and heat can cause insulation to degrade, leading to misfires and check engine lights. Valve cover gasket oil leaks and oil consumption have also been reported. Camshaft and rocker wear can occur, causing a "tapping" sound at idle.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 350/450 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The S 350's M276 V6 and the S 450's M256 inline-six are among Mercedes' most refined petrol engines, but both have well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. The M276 suffers from timing chain tensioner wear and oil cooler seal degradation, while the M256 can develop wiring harness issues and 48V system faults. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner & Cold-Start Rattle
problems.h4: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner & Cold-Start Rattle - The S 350's Signature Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M276's hydraulic secondary chain tensioners can lose oil pressure over time, causing a metallic rattling noise on cold starts. The tensioners have a weak spring and rely on oil pressure to maintain tension. Mercedes issued TSB LI05.10-P-056435 covering updated tensioners and check valves.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace hydraulic tensioners, install check valves per TSB
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early when rattle first appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chains, tensioners, guides, camshaft sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: If rattle has persisted and chain stretch is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded tensioners and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If timing failure has caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2011-2013 S 350 is worth approximately £8,000-£18,000 depending on mileage and condition. The S-Class retains strong residual values - replacement cost is typically justified for well-maintained examples.
problems.recommendation: If your S 350 exhibits a rattling noise on cold start, act immediately. The M276's timing chain tensioners are a known weak point. Specialist tensioner replacement at £700-£1,200 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the chain has stretched or jumped timing, a full rebuilt M276 engine is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M276 Mercedes S 350 engine prices

problems.group: M256 Ignition Coil Wiring Harness Degradation
problems.h4: M256 Ignition Coil Wiring Harness Degradation - The S 450's Electrical Achilles' Heel
problems.rootCause: The M256's ignition coil wiring harness sits close to the turbocharger, and heat can cause the insulation to degrade and crack. This can lead to misfires, check engine lights, and, in severe cases, damage to the engine control unit. The issue affects 2019-2022 M256 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Visual inspection of ignition coil wiring harness
repairOptions.longevity: If warning lights or misfires occur

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace ignition coil wiring harness section with improved heat-resistant design

repairOptions.tier: Major - Full engine wiring harness replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace complete engine wiring harness, ECU inspection
repairOptions.longevity: If widespread harness damage or ECU damage is present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with new wiring harness, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If electrical failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2020-present S 450 is worth approximately £35,000-£60,000 depending on mileage and condition. The S 450 sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: The M256's wiring harness is a known weak point - regular inspection is recommended, especially if you experience misfires or engine warning lights. Replacing the ignition coil harness section at £800-£1,400 is significantly cheaper than a full engine harness replacement. However, if the wiring harness has caused ECU damage, a full rebuilt engine with a new harness is the only safe option. On an S 450 worth £35,000-£60,000, this is a justifiable investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M256 Mercedes S 450 engine prices

problems.group: M256 48V EQ Boost System & Oil Consumption Issues
problems.h4: M256 48V EQ Boost System & Oil Consumption Issues
problems.rootCause: The M256's 48V mild-hybrid system can suffer from battery or ISG (Integrated Starter-Generator) failures, triggering warning lights and loss of EQ Boost assistance. Like many turbocharged engines, the M256 has been reported to consume more oil than expected, potentially due to worn valve cover gaskets, oil cooler leaks, or degraded piston rings.

repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms which component has failed

repairOptions.longevity: If battery has failed causing warning lights

repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is from gasket leaks

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with new 48V components and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If electrical or oil loss has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical S 450 is worth £35,000-£60,000.
problems.recommendation: 48V system faults on the M256 require specialist diagnostics. If you experience oil consumption between services, have the valve cover gaskets and oil cooler inspected. On an S 450 worth £35,000-£60,000, preventative maintenance is always the better investment.

problems.h4: M276 Oil Cooler & Coolant Leak Issues
problems.rootCause: The M276 V6 can suffer from oil cooler seal degradation, causing visible oil leaks and potential mixing of oil and coolant. Coolant hose degradation and leaks from the thermostat housing have also been reported.
